sources.title: Retour des Baléares
sources.creator: Photographer uncredited
sources.researchNote: The caption names the three men on deck and calls de Poligny the director, without naming a film. The occasion can be identified: in 1933 he directed L’Étoile de Valencia, a French version made for the European branch of Universum-Film, whose story runs from a cabaret in Palma to a ship of the same name, with Thomy Bourdelle as Captain Mendoza and Jean Gabin as the ship’s mechanic. The photograph therefore shows the unit returning from the Balearic locations of that film, four months after the French release of the picture he had made with music by Kaper and Jurmann. No photographer or agency is credited beside it.

media.title: Serge de Poligny with Thomy Bourdelle and Jean Gabin — Pour vous, 9 March 1933
media.description: Press photograph published in the film weekly Pour vous on 9 March 1933, captioned “Retour des Baléares. A bord du navire: Bourdelle, le metteur en scène Serge de Poligny et Jean Gabin.” The three are photographed on deck on the way back from the Balearic locations.
media.altText: Three men on a ship’s deck: Thomy Bourdelle in a braided officer’s uniform on the left, Serge de Poligny in a flat cap and sweater with a case on a shoulder strap in the centre, and Jean Gabin in a peaked cap on the right.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph is printed without a photographer’s or agency’s credit and is therefore treated as an anonymous work published in 1933, for which the seventy-year term of protection in France ran out at the end of 2003.
